name: Cagsawa Ruins Park
address: Cagsawa Ruins Road, Brgy. Busay, Daraga, Albay
short: The belfry that survived Mayon's 1814 eruption — and the most photographed Mayon view in the Philippines.
long:
The remains of the Franciscan church complex of Cagsawa, rebuilt in 1724 and destroyed by Mayon Volcano's eruption on 1 February 1814, which killed more than 1,200 people. The surviving belfry, framed by Mayon's near-perfect cone, is one of the most photographed views in the country.

Walk among the walls of the church and convent and the remnants of the Casa Real and Ayuntamiento. The Cagsawa branch of the National Museum holds photographs of past eruptions plus geology and archaeology exhibits.

Cagsawa was declared a National Cultural Treasure in 2015. Its marker was formally unveiled at the opening of the Cagsawa Festival on 1 February 2026, amid talk of a future World Heritage bid. Two more heritage structures inside the complex have been announced as opening soon.
highlights: The 1814 belfry with Mayon behind it
Church and convent walls, Casa Real and Ayuntamiento remnants
Souvenir and food stalls near the entrance
bestTime: Early morning — Mayon is usually clearest before clouds build up around midday
feeNote: Effective 1 July 2026, includes a ₱25 environmental fee. Daraga residents get an extra discount with valid ID. QR passes, digital payments and online booking are available.
safety: Stay on the paths and never climb the stonework. Bring water, a hat and sunscreen — there is little shade at midday.
tips: Allow 60–90 minutes; longer if you add the museum or an ATV ride.
Come early: Mayon is often hidden by clouds by early afternoon.
ATV operators stage just outside — book with DOT-accredited operators only.
verifyNote: New fees relayed from an LGU post by a Bicol blog — confirm with the tourism office.

name: Daraga Church — Our Lady of the Gate Parish
address: Sta. Maria St., Brgy. San Roque (Sta. Maria hill), Daraga, Albay
short: A 1773 volcanic-stone Baroque church on a hill, with Mayon on one side and Albay Gulf on the other.
long:
Built by the Franciscans in 1773 on a hill while Daraga was still a visita of Cagsawa, the church became the main parish after the 1814 eruption and was consecrated to Nuestra Señora de la Porteria (Our Lady of the Gate) in 1854.

Its volcanic-stone Churrigueresque/Baroque façade features four Solomonic (spiral) columns bearing medallions of the Four Evangelists, the Franciscan coat of arms and images of saints. The façade was repaired after World War II. Daraga Church was declared a National Cultural Treasure in 2007.

From the churchyard you can see Mayon on one side and Legazpi and Albay Gulf on the other — one of the best sunrise and sunset spots in town. Visitors also mention a landscaped cascade on the approach.
highlights: Solomonic columns and carved medallions on the façade
Mayon and Albay Gulf views from the churchyard
Sunrise and sunset on the hill
Feast of the patroness every 8 September
bestTime: Sunrise or late afternoon into sunset
tips: Take the stairs beside the Municipal Hall, or drive up to the top.
Dress modestly and keep quiet during Mass.
The LGU noted September 2025 as the 250th celebration of the patroness.

name: Budiao Archaeological Site
address: Brgy. Budiao, Daraga, Albay
short: Ruins of an 18th-century church buried by the 1814 eruption, now being excavated by archaeologists.
long:
The ruins of the Budiao church, part of a pueblo established by decree in 1786, were buried by the 1814 eruption about 7.5 km from Mayon's crater.

The UP Archaeological Studies Program has excavated the site since 2018 with the Diocese of Legazpi and the National Museum. That year, the first Mass in more than two centuries was held among the ruins.

Budiao was declared a local heritage site (SB Resolution 95-2017). In February 2026 the National Museum cited it as one of Daraga's three National Cultural Treasures.
highlights: Part of the 1814 eruption story alongside Cagsawa
One of Daraga's three National Cultural Treasures
safety: Close to the Mayon Permanent Danger Zone. Always check PHIVOLCS and LGU advisories, and confirm with the tourism office whether the site is open to walk-in visitors.
tips: Call the tourism office before going — access depends on the advisory and the excavation schedule.
verifyNote: Exact location unconfirmed — some reports place it toward Bañadero.

name: Mayon Volcano (viewing only)
address: Mayon Volcano Natural Park, Albay
short: A 2,463 m active stratovolcano famous for its near-perfect cone. View it from a distance — entry to the 6-km PDZ is prohibited.
long:
Mayon is an active stratovolcano, 2,463 m high, famed for its near-perfect cone and protected as part of Mayon Volcano Natural Park.

The best views from Daraga are from Cagsawa Ruins, the Daraga Church hill, ATV trail viewpoints and the Bicol International Airport approach.

Entry to the 6-km Permanent Danger Zone is prohibited at all times.
highlights: View from the Daraga Church hill
ATV trail viewpoints (when the advisory allows)
The approach into Bicol International Airport
safety: Do not enter the 6-km Permanent Danger Zone. Follow the current PHIVOLCS alert level. River channels carry lahar risk during heavy rain.
tips: The summit is often clouded after noon — plan photos for the morning.

name: Mayon ATV Adventures (Cagsawa staging area)
address: Cagsawa Road, Brgy. Busay — about 500 m in from Cagsawa Ruins Road, at the parking area
short: Guided ATV rides through lahar channels, river crossings and forest to Mayon viewpoints and old lava flows.
long:
DOT-accredited operators run guided ATV rides from the Cagsawa area through lahar channels, river crossings and forest to viewpoints and old lava flows.

Mayon SkyDrive ATV Adventure lists several trails — including Green Lava, Black Lava (to the 2006 lava wall, about 22 km round trip) and 2018 Lava — plus a "Mayon Hamster Wheel" and a dual zipline. Bicol Adventure ATV and B&B ATV also operate here. The Cagsawa Trail is the cheapest, beginner-friendly option.

Rides usually include a guide/photographer, the ATV and a helmet, but not the environmental fee or transfers.
highlights: Green Lava, Black Lava and 2018 Lava trails
Hamster wheel and dual zipline (Mayon SkyDrive)
bestTime: Early morning for clear views and cooler temperatures
feeNote: Online listings start from about US$47 for the Black Lava trail. Prices vary by operator and trail — confirm before you ride.
safety: Trail availability depends on the PHIVOLCS alert level, LGU advisories and lahar conditions. Some trails approach the Permanent Danger Zone — operators must stay outside it.
tips: Expect touts near Cagsawa — book only with DOT-accredited operators.
Wear clothes you don't mind getting muddy; bring water and sunscreen.

name: FarmPlate
address: Brgy. Gabawan, Daraga, Albay (about 10 minutes from Daraga centro)
short: A farm-themed park with a tiny hilltop chapel, carabao rides, food stalls and a bonfire after dark.
long:
FarmPlate is a farm-themed park that bills itself as "The Happiest Place in Bicol" and "Home of the Smallest Chapel in the Philippines" — the hilltop chapel is its signature photo spot.

Expect a rustic barn, picnic lawns, carabao rides, a kids' play area, and food stalls selling barbecue, wood-fired pizza and buko juice. There is live music and a bonfire in the evening, plus tent and cabin stays.

It is most popular from late afternoon into the night, when the grounds are lit, and especially festive at Christmas. Reviews are mixed on upkeep.
highlights: Evening lights, bonfire and live music
Carabao rides and kids' play area
bestTime: Late afternoon into the evening; December for Christmas displays
feeNote: Adult entrance has been reported at about ₱75–95 (2024–2026 sources differ); kids pay less. Confirm at the gate.
tips: Take a tricycle from Caltex Daraga to Gabawan.

name: Daraga Night Market
address: T. Perez St., from Regidor St. to Rizal St., Poblacion, Daraga
short: A nightly street-food crawl along T. Perez St. — the best place to mingle with locals.
long:
Every night, about 366 m of T. Perez St. — from Regidor St. to Rizal St. — fills with fruit stalls, native food wrapped in banana leaves, grilled street food and late-night eats.

It is the best place in town to mingle with locals, and a short walk from Red Labuyo and the church hill. The LGU and DTI run regular weighing-scale checks at the public and night markets.
bestTime: After dinner — it runs until early morning
tips: Bring small bills — stalls are cash only.

name: Daraga Food Park
address: Rizal St., Brgy. Sagpon, Daraga
short: A casual food park with many stalls — an easy group dinner spot.
long: A casual food-park hangout with multiple stalls under one roof. It is a good pick for group dinners when everyone wants something different.

name: Red Labuyo Restaurant
address: Sta. Maria St., Brgy. San Roque (near Daraga Church), Daraga
short: Mayon-view Bicolano dining near the church — Bicol Express and laing. Ranked #1 in Daraga on Restaurant Guru (2025).
long:
A Mayon-view restaurant on Sta. Maria St., near Daraga Church, serving Bicolano classics such as Bicol Express and laing. It was ranked #1 in Daraga on Restaurant Guru in 2025 and also has rooms.

It's a short walk from the Night Market, so dinner here can roll straight into a street-food crawl.
highlights: Walking distance to the Night Market

name: Balay sa Bikol
address: 1446 Pag-asa St., Daraga
short: Classic Bicolano dishes, top-rated on Tripadvisor and Restaurant Guru — a natural stop after the church.
long: Balay sa Bikol serves classic Bicolano dishes and is top-rated on Tripadvisor and Restaurant Guru. It's often recommended as a lunch stop after visiting Daraga Church.

name: Balay Cena Una
address: F. Lotivio St., Brgy. Bagumbayan, Daraga
short: Fine dining in a restored bahay-na-bato, known for chicken tinutungan and lumpiang tinapa.
long: A restored bahay-na-bato (stone-and-wood house) turned fine-dining restaurant. It's known for its signature chicken tinutungan, lumpiang tinapa and desserts, and in the past it offered a Sunday buffet.
verifyNote: Tripadvisor lists it as temporarily closed — confirm before visiting.

name: Mag'ma Restaurant & Cafe
address: Hotel Herencia 625, Lakandula Dr., Brgy. Bañag, Daraga
short: Asian and Filipino dishes inside Hotel Herencia 625.
long: The in-house restaurant of Hotel Herencia 625, serving Asian and Filipino dishes.

name: Antonia's Restaurant, Cafe & Events Place
short: Filipino restaurant and café that doubles as an events venue.
long: A Filipino restaurant and café that also serves as an events venue.
verifyNote: Directory listing only — address and hours unconfirmed.

name: Jardin del Nuñez
short: A garden restaurant, ranked #3 in Daraga on Restaurant Guru.
long: A garden restaurant ranked #3 in Daraga on Restaurant Guru.

name: 1st Colonial Grill (Daraga branch)
address: Brgy. Sagpon, Daraga
short: Home of sili (chili) ice cream — with heat levels all the way up to "Mayon" — plus Bicolano mains.
long: 1st Colonial Grill invented sili ice cream in 2004, with heat levels up to "Mayon". Other flavours include pili, malunggay and tinutong na bigas (toasted rice). It also serves Bicolano mains and tinapa (smoked fish) twists on staples.
highlights: Pili, malunggay and tinutong na bigas flavours

name: Sizzling Time Daraga
short: Late-night sizzling plates, reportedly open until about 4 AM.
long: Late-night sizzling plates. It has been reported to stay open until about 4 AM.

name: Rose's Kinalas
address: Lotivio St., Daraga
short: Kinalas — noodle soup with a rich broth and shredded meat.
long: A spot for kinalas, the noodle soup with rich broth and shredded meat that originated in Naga and is popular across Albay.

name: Cafe Fabrika
address: L.G. Paran Bldg., Brgy. Kimantong, Daraga (walkable from Daraga Park)
short: A vintage café in a former abaca handicraft factory — art gallery, books, puzzles and free painting.
long: Cafe Fabrika is a vintage café inside a former abaca handicraft factory. It doubles as an art gallery, with vintage collections, souvenirs, books, puzzles and free painting. Regulars recommend the garlic-cheese pizza.

name: 528 Ilawod Cafe
address: Lotivio St., Daraga
short: A home-grown Daraga café (main branch) for coffee, frappes, cakes and pasta.
long: The main branch of a home-grown Daraga café brand, serving coffee, frappes, cakes and pasta. It has since opened branches at SM Legazpi and SM Sorsogon.

name: The Originals Street Cafe
address: Ynez Suites, F. Lotivio St., Brgy. Bagumbayan, Daraga
short: Filipino-inspired menu — tinapa pizza, Bicolana latte and sili latte — with free Wi-Fi.
long: A café with a Filipino-inspired menu: tinapa (smoked fish) pizza and pasta, a Bicolana latte and a sili latte. Free Wi-Fi.

name: Coffee Spot – Daraga
address: Purok 1, Brgy. Tagas (Imelda Roces Ave side), Daraga
short: A café rated for its Mayon views — try the cheesecake and sisig dumplings.
long: A café known for its Mayon views. Visitors recommend the cheesecake and sisig dumplings.

name: Tierra Cafe
address: Rizal St., Brgy. Sagpon, Daraga
short: A cosy matcha-and-coffee spot that's popular on TikTok as a study café.
long: A cosy matcha and coffee spot that's popular on TikTok as a study café.

name: Hotel Herencia 625
address: Lakandula Dr., Brgy. Bañag, Daraga
short: A well-reviewed 3-star hotel (formerly Abaca Suites) minutes from Daraga Church and Cagsawa.
long:
Formerly Abaca Suites, Hotel Herencia 625 is a 3-star hotel with an in-house restaurant (Mag'ma), cooked-to-order breakfast, a 24-hour front desk, free parking, tour assistance and airport transfers. It's minutes from Daraga Church and Cagsawa Ruins.

It holds a Tripadvisor Travelers' Choice award, and a June 2026 Hotels.com review called it "clean and comfortable".

name: Casa Bicolandia Suites
address: Near Daraga Church (about a 10-minute walk, on the hill), Daraga
short: Rooftop Mayon-view terrace, pool and on-site mall, a 10-minute walk from Daraga Church.
long:
Casa Bicolandia Suites has a rooftop restaurant and terrace with Mayon views, an on-site mall, a pool, free parking and Wi-Fi, and it's pet-friendly.

Reviews are mixed: 3/5 on Tripadvisor, while a May 2026 Hotels.com review praised the food and pool.

name: A Traveller's Inn
short: Praised for clean rooms and attentive staff; pet-friendly.
long: Guests praise the clean rooms and attentive staff. Pet-friendly.

name: Daraga Tourist Inn
short: A budget inn about 2.4 miles from Cagsawa Ruins, with free parking.
long: A budget inn about 2.4 miles (3.9 km) from Cagsawa Ruins, with free parking.

name: Y's Rezidenzia Suites
short: Suites that are popular on Traveloka, with free parking.
long: Suites that are popular on Traveloka, with free parking.

name: Casa Lorenzo (Cocotel)
short: Budget-to-mid-range rooms with breakfast.
long: Budget-to-mid-range rooms with breakfast, listed under Cocotel.

name: Casa Basilisa Eco-boutique Resort (Cocotel)
short: A family-friendly eco-boutique resort with a jacuzzi.
long: A family-friendly eco-boutique resort with a jacuzzi, listed under Cocotel.

name: The Oriental Legazpi
address: Taysan hills, Legazpi City (10–20 minutes from Daraga)
short: Hilltop hotel in nearby Legazpi with Albay Gulf and Mayon views and a well-reviewed breakfast.
long: A hilltop hotel in the Taysan hills of Legazpi, 10–20 minutes from Daraga, with views of Albay Gulf and Mayon. Reviewers praise the breakfast spread.

name: Bicol International Airport (DRP)
address: Brgy. Alobo area, Daraga, Albay
short: Bicol's gateway airport, in Daraga — billed as the Philippines' "Most Scenic Gateway" for its Mayon views.
long:
Bicol International Airport (IATA: DRP, ICAO: RPLK) opened in October 2021 in Daraga and is billed as the Philippines' "Most Scenic Gateway" for its Mayon views.

Listed routes include PAL Express and Cebu Pacific from Manila, and Cebgo from Cebu and Iloilo — check airline schedules, as routes change. It's about 15–30 minutes by road to Daraga and Legazpi.
highlights: Flights from Manila, Cebu and Iloilo
tips: Sit on the side facing Mayon when landing for the famous view.
verifyNote: Airline routes change — check current schedules.

name: PNR Daraga Station
address: Market Area, Daraga (South Main Line)
short: Daraga's stop on the PNR South Main Line. Service is intermittent — check PNR advisories.
long: Daraga Station sits in the market area on the Philippine National Railways South Main Line. Service is intermittent: a bridge in Guinobatan was damaged by Typhoon Uwan in November 2025. Check PNR advisories before planning around the train.

name: Daraga Tourism Office (Municipal Hall)
address: Municipal Hall, T. Perez St., Brgy. San Roque, Daraga
short: Ask here about opening hours, fees, guides and anything this site marks "verify".
long: The municipal tourism office is at the Municipal Hall on T. Perez St. The stairs up to Daraga Church start right beside it.
highlights: Stairs to Daraga Church start beside the hall

name: The 7-Eleven with a Mayon backdrop (Camalig)
address: Brgy. Salugan, Camalig, Albay
short: The viral "Philippine Fuji-Lawson" shot — a convenience store with Mayon rising behind it.
long: In April 2025 a 7-Eleven in Brgy. Salugan, Camalig went viral as the Philippine answer to Japan's Mount Fuji Lawson photo, with Mayon rising behind the storefront.
safety: Mind traffic on the highway while taking photos.

name: Camalig day trip
address: Camalig, Albay (next town west of Daraga)
short: Sumlang Lake, Quitinday Hills, Hoyop-Hoyopan Cave, pinangat and the viral 7-Eleven Mayon shot.
long: Daraga's western neighbour makes an easy day trip. Combine Sumlang Lake, the Quitinday (Quintinday) Hills and Hoyop-Hoyopan Cave, eat pinangat — Camalig's famous taro-leaf parcels — and stop for the viral 7-Eleven Mayon photo in Brgy. Salugan.
bestTime: Start early for clear Mayon views
tips: Jovellar's Quitinday Underground River is an option for adventurous travellers.
verifyNote: Outside Daraga — confirm fees and hours with the Camalig tourism office.

name: Legazpi day trip
address: Legazpi City, Albay (north of Daraga)
short: Ligñon Hill, Legazpi Boulevard, the Embarcadero and Albay Park & Wildlife — minutes from Daraga.
long: Albay's capital is right next door. Popular stops include Ligñon Hill, Legazpi Boulevard along Albay Gulf, the Embarcadero and Albay Park & Wildlife.
tips: Jeepneys run between Daraga and Legazpi all day.
verifyNote: Outside Daraga — confirm fees and hours locally.
